overall: A knowledgeable neighbor explaining a city program: curious and lightly dry through the camera gags, then serious and even-handed at the southern Dallas maps question. The read stays level and fair, and settles lower and more certain at the close rather than rising.

lines.text: Since mid-April, fifty bulky trash trucks in Dallas have carried a camera. On their routes, it snaps still photos of the curb.
lines.intent: opens the story with a concrete, odd fact
lines.note: Weight on 'camera'. Plain, curious, like noticing something on the street.

lines.text: Not video. Stills. Each goes to software from a company called City Detect, which looks for trouble.
lines.intent: narrows the claim so nobody over-reads it
lines.note: Weight on 'Stills'. Dry correction, no lift.

lines.text: Tall grass. Weeds. Litter. A car on the lawn. Peeling paint. One house got flagged for its chimney paint.
lines.intent: lists what the software hunts for, ending on the wry chimney
lines.note: Run the list evenly and let the chimney land with a small smile in the voice.

lines.text: The software blurs faces and license plates. One photo the city released had a black box reading motor vehicle.
lines.intent: sets up the privacy promise and the camera gag
lines.note: Weight on 'motor vehicle'. Deadpan, let the absurdity do the work.

lines.text: The blur slips, though. The company says it works about ninety nine percent of the time. When reporters found a plate it missed, the city asked for every photo to go through the blur again.
lines.intent: turns: the safeguard is imperfect, and the fix is honest
lines.note: Weight on 'slips'. Flat on 'ninety nine percent', steady and fair on the redo.

lines.text: In four months, the cameras photographed more than twenty thousand concerns.
lines.note: Weight on 'twenty thousand'. Matter of fact.

lines.text: Too many to read. So each flagged property gets a blight score from one to four, and the photos are ranked so staff know which to look at first.
lines.note: Weight on 'one to four'. Clear and practical, a little quicker than the line before.

lines.text: A flag is not a ticket. A person reviews it. Staff can do nothing, keep watching, send a courtesy notice, ask for an inspection or call a city crew.
lines.intent: separates a flag from a punishment
lines.note: Weight on 'not a ticket'. The reassuring hinge of the film, warm and clear, then the options read as a plain list.

lines.text: A courtesy notice opens no case and sets no deadline. A citation comes only after an officer inspects in person, gives notice, and the problem is still there.
lines.intent: spells out the legal steps precisely
lines.note: Weight on 'only'. Careful, even, no drama.

lines.text: The city's own maps raise a question. Of the 20,000, about 13,800 came from southern Dallas. Could older blocks with less money for repairs get more scrutiny?
lines.intent: raises the maps question, serious and even-handed
lines.note: Weight on 'southern Dallas'. Drop the wryness completely. Land 13,800 and 20,000 quietly. Ask the question straight.

lines.text: Code compliance director Chris Christian says the trucks cover the whole city, and the camera map matches what residents report almost exactly.
lines.note: Weight on 'whole city'. Report it neutrally, no skepticism in the tone.

lines.text: Still, under two percent of southern flags became notices, against more than four percent in the rest of the city. The question stays open.
lines.intent: gives the counter-figure and leaves the question open
lines.note: Weight on 'under two percent'. The quietest, most certain fact of the film. Let 'stays open' sit low and unresolved.

lines.text: Now the notices are changing. They will carry a QR code to a city help page, and council members asked for Spanish versions.
lines.note: Weight on 'QR code'. A modest, forward turn, lighter than the line before.

lines.text: The city says about eight in ten owners fix it after a notice. The camera sees the curb. A person decides what happens next.
lines.note: Weight on 'person'. Slow, settled, landing lower than the middle, dry and sure.
